articles.title: Inde Navarrette on Meeting Pamela Anderson, Hosting ‘SNL’ and X-Men Stunt Training
articles.summary: “Obsession” star Inde Navarrette had quite the busy weekend, going from the Academy Museum Gala on Saturday to the Newport Beach Film Festival on Sunday. Navarrette attended the festival, which runs until Thursday in Newport Beach, as one of Variety’s 10 Actors to Watch, who were celebrated during…
body: Jessica Lange and Pamela Anderson were two of the actresses Navarrette was excited to see Saturday night. “I spoke to Jessica Lange, who is an icon,” she said. “[And] the way that Pamela carries herself with such grace and honesty and just pure creativity and love is just exactly who I want to be.”
And Navarrette’s schedule isn’t slowing down just yet — she’s set to host this year’s “Saturday Night Live” Halloween episode with musical guest Gracie Abrams.

“I literally I feel like I snuck in,” joked the actress. “I’m super excited to keep everything under wraps because I really truly want to make this super fun for the audience. And what I love is when I don’t know anything. So I’m really excited to be working with the writers.”

Also on the horizon is the MCU’s forthcoming “X-Men” film, in which she’ll play Rogue. Navarrette told Malkin she hasn’t corresponded directly with Anna Paquin, who originated the role, but feels “the correspondence started when I was younger, when I really fell in love with the ‘X-Men’ movies in the first place.”

articles.title: ‘The Simpsons’ Surprise: Apu Is Heard for the First Time in Nearly a Decade, as Sunil Malhotra Takes Over for Hank Azaria (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for the Oct. 18 episode of “The Simpsons,” “The Revengening,” which aired Sunday night on Fox. “The Simpsons” has pulled off its own October surprise: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon is back.
body: Also heard on Sunday’s episode was the debut of Janina Gavankar (“The Morning Show”) as Apu’s wife, Manjula. And now that Apu is back and the Kwik-E-Mart has reopened, executive producer Matt Selman said both characters and the Nahasapeemapetilon family will once again be seen (and heard) on “The Simpsons” more often.

“We love this character, and wanted to bring him back in a smart, ‘Simpsons’-y way that allowed him to evolve,” Selman said. “We’re excited by what Sunil has already brought to the role, and look forward to seeing more of Apu in the future.”

Hank Azaria previously voiced Apu, a character that has been controversial over the years due to its stereotypical portrayal of a South Asian convenience store clerk. The issue of Apu was the centerpiece of the 2017 documentary “The Problem With Apu,” in which comedian Hari Kondabolu discussed the impact the character has had on people of South Asian descent.

articles.title: Katseye Says They’re ‘So Proud’ of Sophia Ahead of Her Return to the Group: ‘She’s Our Sister’
articles.summary: Katseye is excited to welcome Sophia Laforteza back to the group after a brief hiatus. Members Lara Raj, Daniela Avanzini, Megan Skiendiel and Yoonchae Jeung shared their support for their “sister” on the carpet at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show on Sunday.
body: The girl group kicked off its “Wildworld” tour in Dublin on Sept. 1, with the first U.S. stop in Miami on Oct. 13. The tour continues across North America through the end of November, with shows in Boston, Montreal, Chicago, Los Angeles and Mexico City.
Laforteza’s step back from the group comes after member Manon Bannerman announced her own temporary hiatus in February. There has been no announcement made about her return to the group.

Katseye formed and gained popularity as K-pop trainees on the 2023 reality competition series “Dream Academy.” Their new documentary, “Katseye: Wild Hearts,” hit Disney+ and Hulu on Oct. 16. The film picks up where Netflix docuseries “Pop Star Academy: Katseye” left off, following the group on their journey to pop stardom after leaving the competition series.

articles.title: Taika Waititi Confirms His ‘Star Wars’ Movie Has Been Put ‘on Ice’ Indefinitely
articles.summary: Taika Waititi’s “Star Wars” movie, which has been in development since 2020, is officially on hold, the director confirmed while promoting his latest film “Klara and the Sun.” “I hate to break this to you, but we’re going to actually put it on ice and we’re working on a different thing together,”…
body: Taika Waititi ’s “Star Wars” movie, which has been in development since 2020, is officially on hold, the director confirmed while promoting his latest film “Klara and the Sun.”

“The stakes are very high, and there’s serious things going on, but there’s also a lot of fun to be had in those films. That’s what I was trying to bring back,” Waititi continued. “I was trying to work in a world that was a little bit separate to that because they’ve got so many things going on within that space. For me to do something there, it would need to be a little different and a little bit more its own thing.”
Previously, exiting Lucasfilm boss Kathleen Kennedy said Waititi’s “Star Wars” was “still somewhat alive.”

Thus far, Waititi’s latest directorial effort, “Klara and the Sun,” has met a mixed response from critics and fans. Variety’ s Guy Lodg e wrote in his review that “Jenna Ortega tries hard to illuminate this misbegotten Kazuo Ishiguro adaptation, but Waititi’s decision to play it for strained, whimsical comedy is ruinous.”
points: Taika Waititi’s “Star Wars” movie, which has been in development since 2020, is officially on hold, the director confirmed while promoting his latest film “Klara and the Sun.

articles.title: Cindy Crawford 'beyond heartbroken' after death of son Presley at 27
articles.summary: Presley Gerber's death in September is being investigated as a suspected overdose.
body: Supermodel Cindy Crawford has said she and her family are "beyond heartbroken" over the death of her son Presley Gerber.

"He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever," she posted on Instagram, next to a black-and-white photo of him. "We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability."
The 27-year-old died on 20 September at a rehab facility in California. Police said officials are investigating his death as a suspected overdose.
Gerber had been a model like his mother and younger sister Kaia, making his catwalk debut for Italian label Moschino aged just 16.

articles.title: Ali G answers his critics: ‘Me ain’t the first intellectual to get haterz’
articles.summary: Staines’s finest nailed the zeitgeist of the late 90s and early 00s, and now he’s back – but how does he fit into 2026? He discusses the backlash against his return, his worst ever interviewee and how he’s going to prevent world war two.
body: “Can you tell people that you’re from Hustler?” Ali G asks me. “Or The Source. Or Guns & Ammo. Speaking to a Guardian journalist ain’t a good look for me in the hood.”

At Ali’s request, we are meeting in an independent chicken shop in Staines because – due to some sort of mix-up – he thought the one interview he had agreed to for his new film was Chicken Shop Date, which was “90% likely to lead to boning”. He follows this with an entirely unprintable reminiscence about the first time he and “me Julie” had sex in the disabled toilets of Egham KFC.

Now that we have established I am not in fact Amelia Dimoldenberg – and that any boning today will be strictly chicken-related – Ali changes tack. Whenever anyone comes near our table, he loudly explains, to my embarrassment, that we are actually conducting a major drug deal. Having seemingly worked his way through the entire menu, he starts asking what else he would need to buy to get the bill up to £500, after discovering that the Guardian is footing it.

articles.title: “Less Red Carpet, More Love of Cinema”: The Warsaw Film Festival Wants to Be a Destination for Discovery
articles.summary: Festival director Joanna Szymańska-Szcześniak and program director Bartek Pulcyn see more room for growth without the glitz and glam: "Our focus is firmly on the quality of the films."
body: The 42nd edition of the Warsaw International Film Festival is screening 190 films, including 132 features, this year. The Polish fest, which opened Oct. 9 with Jesse Eisenberg ’s The Debut, wraps on Sunday. With 102 world, international or regional premieres, the event offers ample opportunity for discoveries, while also screening highlights from this year’s fest circuit.
How do you see Warsaw’s role, vision and positioning in the annual film festival calendar in Eastern Europe and worldwide?

JOANNA SZYMAŃSKA-SZCZEŚNIAK Warsaw has enormous potential as an international film festival destination. We have a city that is developing rapidly, a strong cultural scene and a festival with more than 40 years of history.

When I became general director, I knew I didn’t want to simply maintain what had already been built. I wanted to give the festival new energy and think seriously about where it should be in five or 10 years. For me, that means strengthening our international partnerships, developing our industry activities and making Warsaw an increasingly attractive destination for filmmakers, producers and audiences.
points: Festival director Joanna Szymańska-Szcześniak and program director Bartek Pulcyn see more room for growth without the glitz and glam: "Our focus is firmly on the quality of the films."

articles.title: Marshals Is Putting A Twist One One Of Taylor Sheridan's Yellowstone Traditions
articles.summary: In the third episode of Marshals Season 2, Taylor Sheridan's Yellowstone influence is starting to be felt in the form of a recurring visual motif.
body: "Marshals" Season 2 got off to a disappointing start, but at least the writers are trying to go beyond the show's procedural format by injecting some good old-fashioned Taylor Sheridan-style symbolism. The latest episode of Luke Grimes' "Yellowstone" spin-off confirms that the buffalo Kayce Dutton saw in Episode 2 was much more significant than it seemed. That essentially makes this stoic beast the "Marshals" version of the wolves that hounded Kayce throughout "Yellowstone."

Before his wife Monica Dutton (Kelsey Asbille) was killed off in the worst way possible and Kayce joined the U.S. Marshals, he was struggling to figure out his place in the Dutton Dynasty. Throughout "Yellowstone," his conflict was symbolized by wolves, who showed up at numerous points throughout Sheridan's neo-Western and seemed to portend dark days ahead for John Dutton's (Kevin Costner) youngest son.

articles.title: Jesse Eisenberg Reveals TV Show Details as ‘The Debut’ Closes a Star-Studded London Film Festival
articles.summary: Eisenberg and lead actress Julianne Moore gushed over one another ahead of the well-received screening — and the filmmaker also told THR what his upcoming TV series is about.
body: Jesse Eisenberg and Julianne Moore were full of love for each other as their latest team-up, The Debut, closed this year’s BFI London Film Festival.

Eisenberg sat down for a Screen Talk session earlier in the day, where he revealed the film would simply not have been made without Moore’s involvement and spoke at length about his own relationship growing up in community theater. “I love it more than I’ve ever loved anything I’ve made,” the director and Social Network, Zombieland and Now You See Me actor told The Hollywood Reporter on the red carpet. “It has everything that I love in a project. It has music, and it has absurdism, and it has heart, and it has depressed people, but in funny situations. It’s my favorite thing in the world.”

articles.title: Before Clayface, Tom Rhys Harries Was In A Little-Discussed Fantasy Movie With Patrick Stewart
articles.summary: There are far more Dragonheart films than you realize, and one of these fantasy flicks stars a pre-Clayface Tom Rhys Harries opposite Patrick Stewart.
body: There are five films in the "Dragonheart" film series. Yes, seriously. And yes, Tom Rhys Harries — the star of DC Studios' Batman-adjacent horror movie "Clayface" – plays a lead in the fourth of them, "Dragonheart: Battle for the Heartfire," opposite Patrick Stewart, who played the voice of Draco the dragon. No one talks about this movie (or any of the other "Dragonheart" sequels or prequels, either).

Some readers may recall Rob Cohen's original 1996 film "Dragonheart" with clarity. Dennis Quaid stars as Sir Bowen, a knight in the 10th Century who has sworn to hunt down and slay all the dragons. His quest is successful, and the bulk of the movie concerns Bowen's relationship to Draco (Sean Connery), the last living dragon. It's a fun flick, it made a decent chunk of change, and it was nominated for Best Visual Effects at the Academy Awards. Most folks rank it among the best movies about dragons ever made.
